Left translation multiplies by an invertible operator. For a pure normalized support the scalar 1+ζ^{ka}+ζ^{kb} vanishes exactly when its final two terms are the opposite primitive cube roots. Bezout for gcd(a/d,b/d,2n/d)=1 forces k to have order three modulo M; the opposite residue condition admits both such k, with d lifts each and two kernel directions per lift. A mixed block has determinant |1+ζ^{ka}|²−(−1)^k. Odd blocks are invertible; even blocks lose one rank at each of the 2d solutions of the two cube-root congruences exactly when 3|n/d. This also handles a=n (no singularity). For eligible mixed d there are 2φ(n/d) admissible differences; count ordered pairs and singleton then divide by two. Proof line 84's phrase 'for each divisor' overstates the raw nonzero-difference count for d=n, where there is one; this ineligible class is never used in the census. For the pure side count primitive ordered pairs with opposite nonzero residues modulo three by CRT, multiply by 4n base points and divide by six; the gcd and residue class are invariant under reanchoring. Summing the mixed totients gives 8n³(1−3^−v); summing the pure local factors gives (2n³/3)(1−3^−2v). Maximal d=2n/3 in the pure case forces the subgroup cosets and beats the mixed maximum 2n/3.
